lines.ruling: Ruling: scope; i4562 p. 5, Line 12: "The limitations on lines 5 and 11 apply to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity. Therefore, if you have more than one business or activity, you may allocate your allowable section 179 expense deduction among them." The candidate is true on every return with more than one Schedule C, so Schedule C refuses there even with no section 179 deduction to allocate (classm.f8995.3: two Schedules C, lines 8, 10 and 12 $0.00, Form 1040 line 37 computed; project false, candidate true). The project refuses only when line 12 differs from the 2025 elections (line 8) and there is more than one Schedule C; otherwise each business deducts its own elections, an allocation the "may allocate" sentence permits, so the project computes correctly where the candidate refuses and the candidate names no condition the project misses. Ruling: ambiguity; i4562 p. 4, Line 1: "Generally, the maximum section 179 expense deduction is $2,500,000 for section 179 property (including qualified section 179 real property) placed in service during the tax year beginning in 2025."; "Tip: You can use Worksheet 1 to assist you in determining the amount to enter on line 1."; Worksheet 1: "3. Enter the smaller of line 1 or line 2 here ... 4. Enter the amount from line 3 here and on Form 4562, line 1". amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property records the Worksheet 1 cost cap as the alternative reading; the owner adopted line 1 as the $2,500,000 the line 1 instruction states (TASKS T-043, research memo ambiguities/research/amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property.md: with that line 1, lines 5 to 12 compute 26 U.S.C. 179(b)(3)(B) exactly, while the cap changes no return without a carryover and withholds a carryover on a return with no 2025 property, e.g. stage14.s179.carryover_no_property). The candidate-refuses and candidate-unknown records arise because the candidate's line 1 reads line 2: cited refusals (scveh.low_use, scveh.screened, asset.screened, asset.listed_low) and the Schedule C roster on returns the full interview refuses or leaves incomplete, which the project's own line 2 reads too. Project stands under the owner's ruling.

Ruling: model error; i4562 p. 5, Line 11, Individuals: "Also, include all wages, salaries, tips, and other compensation you earned as an employee (from Form 1040, line 1a)." The candidate omits Form 1040 line 1a and uses only the Schedule C income before the section 179 deduction. Example: stage14.s179.wages_count (Schedule C income before section 179 $3,000, wages $20,000): project line 11 $23,000.00 (fixture expectation), candidate $3,000.00 by its expression, so its line 12 would be $3,000 instead of $10,000. Many value differences also pass through line 5, the consequence of the line 1 reading ruled ambiguity (amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property), and those are not this error. This is a separate source error from the line 1 ambiguity, whose register entry does not cover wages.
